title: External audit plan and third quarter budget report
subtitle: Paramedic facility funding, life-saving recognitions, and a staff recognition for a national committee of adjustment association role.
overview: The committee received KPMG LLP's 2024 External Audit Plan for information {{vote:m1}}. The plan sets out how the auditors will test the city's 2024 financial statements. Year-end testing is planned for March to June, with a report back to the committee afterward.

On the consent agenda, the committee recommended approval of the 2024 Third Quarter Budget Monitoring Report's funding adjustments, along with a $448 thousand budget adjustment for the Paramedics Facility Renewal project {{vote:m2}}. Because this is a committee recommendation, Council still needs to adopt it. For residents, it shows the city's operating budget tracking close to forecast.

The meeting also included recognitions. A staff member was congratulated on becoming president of the Ontario Association of Committees of Adjustment and Consent Authorities. Community members, YMCA employees and paramedics were thanked for life-saving responses to two cardiac emergencies. The meeting adjourned at 2:45 p.m.

decisions.detail: The committee received KPMG LLP's 2024 External Audit Plan for information {{vote:m1}}.

The committee recommended approving the funding adjustments in Table 4 of Attachment 2 to the 2024 Third Quarter Budget Monitoring Report, and a $448 thousand budget adjustment for Paramedics Facility Renewal {{vote:m2}}.

debate: On audit materiality, one councillor asked what lowering the threshold would mean. The auditor said a lower threshold would mean more testing, for example larger sample sizes and more detailed analytical checks. The auditor also said every transaction is subject to testing, not only those above the threshold.
A councillor said the materiality level seemed high compared with thresholds used by other organizations. The auditor's explanation that smaller items are still tested addressed that concern.

On the use of AI in audits, the auditor described tools that scan full sets of transactions and journal entries for outliers and high-risk items. The auditor said most audit work is still done on site by people, and a councillor agreed that on-site presence is valuable.

On development charges, a councillor asked how collections affect reserves over time. The auditor said the audit looks at the year's activity, not whether reserves are sufficient. Staff added that reserves are reported annually in May and that development charge collections and exemptions are now reported quarterly.

On the budget report, one councillor praised the result as being within a small margin of forecast, a surplus under $1 million on a roughly half-billion-dollar operating budget. The councillor also noted the report's transparency. Another councillor agreed.
